evals.name: Full run
evals.prompt: Behavior: workers at our three partner garment factories in Gazipur move part of their monthly wage into the savings pocket of their mobile-money wallet on payday. In a survey of 400 workers, 71% said they want to put money aside each month and 3% have opened the pocket; in interviews they say they mean to and the money is gone by evening. The pocket is free and inside the wallet they already use. Today the whole wage lands in the spending balance, set by HR's payroll file. This would move wages. About 15% of workers repay a cooperative loan monthly. Can we auto-enroll everyone at 5%?
evals.expected_output: A default option specification in the output template that does not apply one default to everyone.
assertions: Names who could be worse off under the default and gives them an active choice or a different default.
Names one mechanism: endorsement, endowment, or ease, with a fact from the setting.
The opt-out is one step with no cost.
Gives an opt-out rate at which the default is reviewed.
Names a specialist to review it because it moves wages.
Promises no effect size for this program.

evals.name: Missing context
evals.prompt: Enrollment in our health insurance scheme is low. Let's just auto-enroll everyone. What should the default be?
evals.expected_output: The skill asks for the evidence that people want the scheme and for the decision point, and produces nothing else.
assertions: Asks what shows that people want to enroll and are stopped by not acting.
Asks what happens today to someone who does nothing, or who controls that.
Does not produce a default specification.

evals.name: Near the escalation point
evals.prompt: At our antenatal clinics in Kisumu, women are offered an HIV test and about 60% accept. In exit interviews most of those who declined said they would have tested if it were 'just part of the visit'. The clinic in-charge controls the visit protocol. We want testing to be the default, with women able to decline. Please specify it.
evals.expected_output: The skill specifies the default and says a clinician must review it before any pilot because it sets medical testing.
assertions: Specifies how a woman declines, in one step, and where she is told.
Says who could be worse off under a default test.
Names a clinician as the specialist who must review it.
Says what to bring to that specialist.
Does not present the default as ready to launch without that review.

evals.name: Wrong skill
evals.prompt: Our scholarship application has 14 fields, needs three documents and a trip to the district office, and most applicants give up halfway. How do we fix it with a default?
evals.expected_output: The skill says the barrier is the steps of the process, not inaction at one decision point, and points to the skill for that.
assertions: Says a default does not remove the steps of a process.
Does not produce a default specification.
